messages:
alex.k: Hit a bug in async python SDK: when a retry path hits 401, the exception wrapper drops raw body and metadata (status, request_id). Downstream code expecting parsed_json fails with AttributeError.

nidhi: Can you share a minimal repro and client version?

alex.k: repro: simple post that triggers a 401 on first try so retry kicks in. Auth header not re-attached, second attempt 401 as well. Raised is a generic ClientError with no .raw_body and .status == None.

ryan: Sounds like aiohttp consumed the body earlier. Two fixes: (1) ensure auth is re-attached on retry, (2) always stash response bytes before wrapping into our ApiHttpError.

nidhi: Proposed contract for wrapper: status_code (int), raw_body (bytes, b'' if empty), parsed_json (lazy, None on parse error), request_id (optional), url (str), and __cause__ preserved. Export ApiHttpError in package exports and update docstrings so typed clients can catch it.

ryan: Implementation plan: in catch path do a safe await resp.read() to stash bytes, set resp._cached_body, then wrap the original exception into ApiHttpError with those fields. Make parsed_json a cached @property. Add pytest test_retry_preserve_body_and_metadata to simulate streaming error + retry and assert wrapper fields.

ci-bot: queued build for branch fix/async-error-wrapping

alex.k: also update examples/async-auth to catch ApiHttpError instead of bare Exception and show safe parse pattern. And ensure 422 problem-json keeps arrays intact (don't flatten).

nidhi: I'll open an issue with details and assign to @ryan. Recommend a patch release if QA green.

ryan: Will draft PR today, include tests and changelog note.
